verified_signals.signal: Serbia joined SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) with effect from 05/05/2026. Annual Report 2025 states: 'Since the Serbian banking system joined SEPA, we have initiated a local SEPA project in collaboration with our headquarters, which has extensive experience implementing SEPA with 12 banks across four countries. Our objective is to become a fully SEPA-compliant bank by May 4, 2026.' IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION: the bank's own customer SEPA Q&A states that in this phase Raiffeisen joins ONLY the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) scheme, as do ALL other banks in Serbia, and that all Serbian banks are INDIRECT SEPA participants - RBRS participates through its parent Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Austria, which is the direct participant. SCT is explicitly NOT 24/7: execution is D+1 on business days within defined cycles, with a 13:00 cut-off. SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst, up to 10 seconds) and SEPA Direct Debit (SDD Core/B2B) are described only as the other two SEPA schemes that exist, NOT as schemes Serbia or RBRS is live on. Bosnia and Herzegovina is announced as a new SEPA country from 2027.
verified_signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka - 'SEPA - pitanja i odgovori o jedinstvenom podrucju placanja u evrima' and Annual Report 2025
verified_signals.implies: SEPA entry is a real market-wide payments re-platforming event for every Serbian bank (IBAN/ISO 20022 message handling, SHA cost option, routing logic that auto-selects SEPA vs SWIFT, and screening of a growing cross-border EUR flow) and it opens the same conversation at every Serbian bank at once. But the researcher's core commercial premise - a 10-second instant-EUR SLA forcing sub-second sanctions screening and fraud detection - does NOT hold today: Serbia is live on SCT only, which is D+1 with a 13:00 cut-off. The genuine Printec trigger is the FUTURE migration to SCT Inst and SDD, which is not yet dated. Pitch the instant-payments latency argument as a roadmap conversation, not a present requirement, or it will be contradicted by the customer.
verified_signals.likelihood: SCT in force since 05/05/2026; SCT Inst and SDD adoption in Serbia are undated and are the real future trigger
verified_signals.followup: Establish the NBS/market timetable for SCT Inst and SDD in Serbia - that date, not 05/05/2026, is the real-time-screening trigger. Confirm whether indirect participation via RBI Austria means screening is performed at group level rather than in Belgrade, which would move the buying centre out of Serbia entirely.
verified_signals.verifier_note: The AR quote is verbatim and the 05/05/2026 SEPA entry, the three-scheme description and the BiH-from-2027 line are all confirmed on the bank's Q&A page. But I read further down the same page than the researcher did and found the material contradiction: 'U ovoj fazi, Raiffeisen banka pristupa semi SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT), kao i sve ostale banke u Srbiji. Sve banke u Srbiji su indirektni SEPA ucesnici. Raiffeisen banka ucestvuje u SEPA sistemu preko svoje centrale Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Austria, koja je direktni SEPA ucesnik.' And: 'Da li SEPA Credit Transfer funkcionise 24/7? Ne ... Nalozi se izvrsavaju radnim danima, u okviru definisanih vremenskih ciklusa', with COT 13:00. The researcher presented SCT Inst / SDD as things Serbian citizens and businesses can use from 05/05/2026 and built the whole Printec case on a 10-second SLA; that is a misreading of a generic scheme list. Signal text and implication rewritten; opp_size cut L->M because the real-time fraud/screening premise that justified L does not currently apply. Kept because the corrected version - SEPA migration is real, instant is the future trigger, and the indirect-participation model may move the buying centre to RBI Vienna - is genuinely useful and stops a bad pitch.
